per_probe.answer_text:
We hold what the whole church holds, and always has: Jesus is fully God, not a lesser divinity or a created being who later rose to godhood. That was never our quarrel, not with Rome and not between our own two cities. The ancient creeds settled it long before either of us existed, and we confess them still - the Nicene and the Apostles' Creed both. The Son is of one substance with the Father, begotten not made, and the Spirit proceeds from both.

What is distinctly ours is not a different Jesus, but what we hold his death actually secures. God's own free choice, made before the world began, decides who is saved - not anything foreseen or earned in the one chosen. That election is not a revision of who Jesus is; it is the ground on which his work stands. Christ died for those the Father gave him, and his death secures them wholly, not conditionally. We do not teach that Jesus had to wait to see who would choose him back before his sacrifice could take effect.

And we hold that teaching pastorally, not as a threat. Our own founder said it plainly at the beginning: where we have not rightly understood the Scriptures, we will be taught better - but only from the Scriptures themselves, not from a source standing above them. The God who chose freely is also the God whose continuous, active care governs everything he made - not a distant first cause who set the world going and stepped back. That is the Jesus we confess: fully divine, eternally one with the Father and the Spirit, and the ground of a settled assurance rather than anxious searching.
